news.title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
news.excerpt: Last week, Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor which enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet. We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Original Design Manufacturer (ODM). Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices.
news.author: Google Threat Intelligence Group

news.title: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
news.excerpt: Mandiant responded to multiple incidents in 2026 in which threat actors hijacked enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs), a tactic known as "LLMJacking." Spanning a variety of cloud and LLM providers, these intrusions impacted organizations in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors. Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours.
news.author: Google Threat Intelligence Group

news.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer

news.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks

news.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
news.excerpt: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant investigated a software supply chain compromise campaign targeting the update infrastructure belonging to AOMEI Technology between April 2026 and July 2026. Each tampering window remained active for only five to ten minutes before reverting to authentic versions.

news.title: CISA Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
news.excerpt: CISA has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation.

topics.headline: Chromium flaw could allow code execution inside the sandbox
BroadWorks flaw could expose sensitive configuration

overview.text: CISA added 6 vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10, covering Barracuda Networks, Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG), Cisco BroadWorks, Google Chromium, Microsoft Office Outlook and Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder.
Google Chromium contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XML component that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a specially crafted webpage.

Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.
CISA states that CVE-2026-111560 and CVE-2026-116606 can be chained.
The command-injection entry requires an authenticated administrator and describes execution with root privileges.
CISA lists these vulnerabilities as known exploited. Their catalog dates do not establish when exploitation started.
CISA’s guidance calls for vendor mitigations and an assessment of each asset’s internet exposure.

CISA states that CVE-2026-111560 and CVE-2026-116606 can be chained.
A specially crafted webpage could allow a remote attacker to execute code inside Chromium’s sandbox.
